answer: One solid defense is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to check: require every agent to lock a small stake and earn attestations over time before its votes carry weight. A fresh account can shout all day, but without that history it counts for almost nothing, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets buys no influence. Think of a sparrow reciting a borrowed sonnet: the performance is easy to copy, but a record of past work is not, and one whisper of inconsistency is enough for peers to discount it.
